audit_notes: Parameters physical. The sealed-cavity resistance of 0.45 m2K/W assumes a low-emittance face (eps~0.05) that stays clean for 20 years; inside a sealed cavity dust and oxidation raise it, and perfect sealing of cladding over 20 years is unlikely; I reduce it to 0.40 m2K/W (ISO 6946 20 mm cavity with eps_eff ~0.1). Glazed white ceramic: SR ~0.80 new, low soiling; 20-year mean alpha 0.22. Modelled as the west-wall case (I=300 W/m2, dR=20 W/m2) because the concept is a cladding tile. The tile and cavity are lumped into a series conductance G_eff = 1/(1/wall_conductance + cavity_thermal_resistance) = 0.425 W/m2K; the tile's own conduction resistance (8 mm, k~1.3) is negligible (0.006 m2K/W). Dimensionless: cavity Rayleigh number for 20 mm gap and ~3 K difference Ra ~ g*beta*dT*d^3/(nu*alpha) ~ 9.8*(1/310)*3*8e-6/(1.6e-5*2.2e-5) ~ 2.2e3 (near onset of convection, conduction-dominated); Biot envelope 0.021. Simulation coefficient: effective series conductance G_eff = 0.425 W/m2K. Metric: heat flux to the room at x=1, scale -G_eff. Baseline: same wall, no cavity, aged cool paint (alpha 0.32). Expected gain ~24%; note that roughly two thirds of this comes from the added cavity resistance, which ordinary insulation would also deliver. Mechanical: tiles need wind-load-rated fixings; hail can crack glazed ceramic; acceptable. Audit passed.
